text:
alex: FYI I pulled a community fork of Lumen-70B for offline evals. Their model card links to a license that looks like CC-BY-NC with an extra sentence about not redistributing weights — can we run quant/serve this in the hosted catalog?

maya: what does the exact license text say? NC will block commercial use for sure. 'no-weights-redistribution' could be stricter. paste pls

alex: here's the snippet from their repo: `
"Licensed under CC-BY-NC-4.0. Model weights may be used for research and evaluation only. Redistribution of model weights or converted formats is prohibited without express permission from the authors."
`

rachel (Legal): ok two separate things: (1) NC = non-commercial: prohibits using the model to provide paid services or features to customers. (2) the explicit no-redistribution clause means we cannot distribute the weights or derived binaries (including quantized checkpoints) to third parties without permission.

tomas: so hosting behind our API (hosted inference) — is that redistribution? i think not if we don't hand out the weights. but Dedicated/private customers who want on-prem or VPC copies would need the weights -> problem

maya: also note that quantized artifacts are "derived" under most licenses, so creating a q4/q8 version and shipping it would likely be redistribution. Even if we only keep quant locally, providing a downloadable bundle to a customer is a violation.

rachel (Legal): correct. If we only provide hosted inference (our servers) and do not expose the weights or let customers run them locally, that mitigates redistribution risk. But NC still forbids commercial use, so we'd need exception/permission for any paid usage. For internal evals or unpaid community trials it's probably ok.

alex: proposed path: (a) mark this model "compliance: restricted" in the onboarding tracker, (b) block adding to public model-catalog until legal sign-off, (c) allow hosted-internal eval only, no dedicated/private deploy. approved?

maya: +1. for evals we need quant tests though — can we run quant privately on our infra without distributing? i.e. q it for speed tests but never expose the artifact externally

rachel (Legal): running quant internally for research/eval is allowed under the quoted clause, assuming you're not distributing the quantized files. Keep a clear chain-of-custody log and don't share artifacts. I'll need the repo link and author contact so we can ask for a commercial/redistribution exception if we want to ship to customers.

tomas: noted. I'll add a policy flag in model-ops: `hosted-only`, `no-redistribute`, `nc-licensed`. That will prevent adding to Dedicated/Private catalogs automatically.

model-ops-bot: :information_source: Model onboarding blocked by compliance: set status -> compliance_pending. Ticket #INF-4127 created.

alex: adding the repo link and author email to INF-4127 now. rachel — can you draft a short permission request template we can send?

rachel (Legal): yes. I'll DM a template, includes: intended commercial use, redistribution/format conversion ask, and whether they'd accept a paid license or contributor agreement. Also include attribution language required (author name, repo link, license text).

alex: perfect. for the model-card we'll add an explicit attribution blurb and a warning: "Not cleared for commercial or redistributed use; hosted inference only until permission obtained."

maya: sounds good. i'll run internal q4 tests and keep the artifacts local, will upload perf numbers to the ticket only.

rachel (Legal): thanks. once we get explicit permission we can reassess for Dedicated/private. Until then treat as research-only.

alex: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
